name: Cairo
summary: Cairo — al-Qāhira, ‘the Victorious’ — is the largest city in the Arab world and in Africa, strung along the Nile where the river fans into its delta. It is a city in layers: the pharaonic pyramids of Giza on its western horizon, a Roman fortress and Coptic churches at its old core, a thousand-year-old Islamic capital of minarets and madrasas at its heart, and a restless megacity of some 22 million on top. Egyptians call it Umm al-Dunya — the Mother of the World.

figures.label: Population
figures.note: City proper; ≈22 million in Greater Cairo — the largest metropolis in the Arab world and Africa.

figures.label: al-Qāhira founded
figures.note: By the Fatimids. Predecessors: Fustat (641) and Memphis nearby (c. 3100 BC).

figures.label: Setting
figures.note: Where the river fans out just north of the city.

figures.label: World Heritage
figures.note: One of the world’s oldest Islamic cities, with its famous mosques and madrasas.

figures.label: On the horizon
figures.note: Older than the medieval city beside them by roughly 2,500 years.

events.title: Memphis, first capital
events.body: Memphis is founded nearby as capital of a newly unified Egypt.

events.title: The Great Pyramid
events.body: The Great Pyramid of Khufu rises at Giza.

events.title: Persia conquers Egypt
events.body: Persia conquers Egypt; the age of native pharaohs wanes.

events.title: Cleopatra and Roman Egypt
events.body: Cleopatra dies; Egypt becomes a Roman province and Rome’s granary.

events.title: The Arab conquest and Fustat
events.body: Arab armies under ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs take Egypt and found Fustat.

events.title: The Fatimids found Cairo
events.body: The Fatimids conquer Egypt and found al-Qāhira — Cairo.

events.title: Al-Azhar is founded
events.body: Al-Azhar mosque and university is founded, a beacon of learning.

events.title: Badr al-Jamali's walls
events.body: The vizier Badr al-Jamali rebuilds Cairo’s walls and monumental gates.

events.title: Fustat is burned
events.body: Fustat is burned to deny it to the Crusaders threatening Cairo.

events.title: Saladin ends Fatimid rule
events.body: Saladin ends Fatimid rule and founds the Ayyubid dynasty.

events.title: Saladin's Citadel begins
events.body: Saladin begins the great Citadel on the Mokattam spur.

events.title: The Mamluks seize power
events.body: The Mamluks — a caste of freed slave-soldiers — seize power in Cairo.

events.title: Victory at Ain Jalut
events.body: The Mamluks halt the seemingly invincible Mongols at Ain Jalut.

events.title: The Black Death
events.body: The Black Death reaches Cairo, killing perhaps a third of its people.

events.title: The Ottoman conquest
events.body: The Ottomans defeat the Mamluks; Egypt becomes an Ottoman province.

events.title: Napoleon takes Cairo
events.body: Napoleon takes Cairo after the Battle of the Pyramids.

events.title: The French are expelled
events.body: British and Ottoman forces expel the French from Egypt.

events.title: Muhammad Ali seizes power
events.body: Muhammad Ali Pasha seizes power and founds modern Egypt.

events.title: Massacre at the Citadel
events.body: Muhammad Ali massacres the Mamluk beys at the Citadel, ending their power.

events.title: ‘Paris on the Nile’
events.body: Khedive Ismail begins remaking Cairo with grand boulevards — “Paris on the Nile.”

events.title: The Suez Canal opens
events.body: The Suez Canal opens amid lavish Cairo celebrations.

events.title: Britain occupies Egypt
events.body: Britain crushes the Urabi revolt and occupies Egypt.

events.title: The Egyptian Museum opens
events.body: The Egyptian Museum opens on Tahrir Square.

events.title: The 1919 revolution
events.body: A nationwide uprising demands independence from Britain.

events.title: A kingdom’s independence
events.body: Egypt gains nominal independence as a kingdom.

events.title: The first Arab–Israeli war
events.body: Egypt joins the first Arab–Israeli war.

events.title: The Free Officers’ revolution
events.body: The Free Officers depose the king; the monarchy falls.

events.title: Nasser nationalises the Canal
events.body: Nasser nationalises the Suez Canal, triggering an international crisis.

events.title: The Six-Day War
events.body: The Six-Day War ends in a shattering Egyptian defeat.

events.title: The Aswan High Dam
events.body: The Aswan High Dam is completed, ending the Nile’s ancient flood.

events.title: The funeral of Umm Kulthum
events.body: The funeral of the singer Umm Kulthum draws millions into Cairo’s streets.

events.title: The bread riots
events.body: “Bread riots” erupt across Cairo against cuts to food subsidies.

events.title: Sadat is assassinated
events.body: President Sadat is assassinated at a Cairo military parade.

events.title: The 1992 earthquake
events.body: An earthquake kills over 500 people and topples old buildings.

events.title: Tahrir Square and Mubarak's fall
events.body: The Tahrir Square uprising forces Hosni Mubarak from power.

events.title: The upheaval of 2013
events.body: Mass protests and a military takeover convulse the capital.

events.title: A new capital in the desert
events.body: Ground is broken on a vast New Administrative Capital east of Cairo.

events.title: The Pharaohs’ Golden Parade
events.body: Twenty-two royal mummies are paraded in a golden convoy to a new museum.

places.name: Giza pyramids
places.note: The pyramids of Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure, on the desert edge west of the city.

places.name: Fustat (Old Cairo)
places.note: The first Arab capital of Egypt (641) and the Coptic core.

places.name: Al-Azhar
places.note: Mosque and university founded 970–972, a millennium-old seat of learning.

places.name: The Citadel
places.note: Saladin’s fortress on the Mokattam spur, begun 1176.

places.name: Tahrir Square
places.note: The civic heart of modern Cairo and the Egyptian Museum.

places.name: Khan el-Khalili
places.note: The great medieval bazaar of Islamic Cairo.

caveats: This timeline is compiled from general reference works — listed under Sources — rather than an event-by-event archive of primary documents, as the Mumbai timeline is. Treat it as a reliable outline, not a citation of record.
Dates for the earliest, legendary events are traditional rather than documented.

dynasties.note: The dynasties that built and ruled Cairo, from the Fatimid founders to the makers of modern Egypt.

list.name: The Fatimids
list.summary: A Shia Ismaili dynasty that founded al-Qāhira as an imperial capital and established Al-Azhar. At their height they ruled from North Africa to Syria and the Hejaz and claimed the caliphate itself.

list.name: The Ayyubids
list.summary: Founded by Salah al-Din, who ended Fatimid rule, restored Sunni Islam in Egypt, built the Citadel and led the Muslim recovery of Jerusalem.

list.name: The Mamluks
list.summary: A self-perpetuating caste of freed military slaves who governed Egypt from Cairo, broke the Mongols and the Crusaders, and endowed the city with its finest mosque-madrasa architecture.

list.legacy: The Egyptian state, and ‘Paris on the Nile’
list.name: The Muhammad Ali dynasty
list.summary: Founded by Muhammad Ali Pasha, the architect of modern Egypt, who massacred the Mamluk beys to seize power. His line of khedives and kings ruled until the 1952 revolution.
